entries.title: Blackhawks' Connor Bedard suffers apparent left shoulder injury training in Vancouver
entries.summary: <p>While the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks?_gl=1*jdrb1j*_up*MQ..*_ga*MTcwODM1NjU5OS4xNzgzMDM4MDk4*_ga_K0F0MB46T8*czE3ODMwMzgwOTgkbzEkZzAkdDE3ODMwMzgxMDEkajU3JGwwJGgw" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> try to figure out Connor Bedard's contract and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/07/02/blackhawks-first-line-hole-connor-bedard-kyle-davidson-nhl-trades?_gl=1*1w7fxke*_up*MQ..*_ga*MTcwODM1NjU5OS4xNzgzMDM4MDk4*_ga_K0F0MB46T8*czE3ODMwMzgwOTgkbzEkZzAkdDE3ODMwMzgwOTgkajYwJGwwJGgw" target="_blank" >linemates</a> for next season, they might also need to worry about Bedard himself.</p><p>The Hawks' cornerstone star suffered an apparent left shoulder injury while skating Thursday in his hometown of Vancouver.</p><p>A video of the incident shows Bedard losing his balance and falling into the boards, then quickly skating off the ice holding his left shoulder in apparent pain.</p><p>It looked similar to how Bedard skated off the ice Dec. 12 in St. Louis after <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2025/12/15/blackhawks-connor-bedard-injury-update-surgery-nick-foligno?_gl=1*8gflsx*_up*MQ..*_ga*MTY5Mjc1MDQ1MS4xNzgzMDM4MjIw*_ga_K0F0MB46T8*czE3ODMwMzgyMjAkbzEkZzAkdDE3ODMwMzgyMjAkajYwJGwwJGgw" target="_blank" >injuring</a> his right shoulder — the opposite shoulder — on a final-second faceoff against the Blues. Ryan McGregor, a Hawks blogger watching the practice Thursday in Vancouver, first reported the news and described it as reminiscent of the St. Louis incident.</p><p>Bedard missed four weeks of games as a result of that injury, but he wasn't 100% — and wasn't able to take faceoffs — for his first month back in the lineup. It wasn't until the end of the Olympic break, more than two months after the injury, that he appeared back to 100%.</p><p>If Thursday's injury follows the same timeline, Bedard would theoretically be healthy for the start of training camp in mid-September. But his offseason training could be disrupted, and the pattern of shoulder injuries could also be concerning long-term.</p><p>Bedard's agent, Don Meehan, did not immediately respond to a request for information Thursday. Bedard is also currently without a contract as a restricted free agent, although his camp and the Hawks have been <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/06/23/connor-bedard-blackhawks-contract-negotiations-nhl-free-agency-leo-carlsson-adam-fantilli" target="_blank" >negotiating</a>.</p>

entries.title: Former Bulls coach Billy Donovan joins Spurs staff: report
entries.summary: <p>Former <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bulls" >Bulls</a> head coach Billy Donovan has found a new NBA home. </p><p>The San Antonio Spurs have added Donovan to their coaching staff, per ESPN's Shams Charania.</p><p>Donovan had spent the last 11 seasons as a head coach in Oklahoma City and Chicago, but will now take a step back, operating as the Spurs' "lead assistant coach" under head coach Mitch Johnson.</p><p>The Spurs lost to the 2026 NBA Finals to the Knicks in five games. </p><p>The Bulls announced Donovan's departure from the team on April 21 after entries.title: Davis Martin's struggles expose bullpen in White Sox' walk-off loss to Guardians
entries.summary: <p>CLEVELAND — The White Sox hope right-hander Davis Martin gets to pitch in the All-Star Game, but they’re not going to change their rotation to allow that to happen.</p><p>“That’s not something that we’re doing anything to adjust for,” manager Will Venable said.</p><p>After Davis’ latest stinker on the road — which resulted in a 6-5, walk-off loss to the Guardians on Thursday night — that point might be moot.</p><p>Though three relievers combined to give up a three-run lead, capped by Brayan Rocchio’s two-run homer in the ninth inning off Grant Taylor, Davis put the bullpen in a tough spot. He matched a season low with 3 ⅓ innings and failed to strike out anyone for the first time as a starter. He left with the Sox trailing 2-0.</p><p>Davis’ home-road splits are stark. In seven starts at Rate Field, he has an 0.88 ERA with a 0.951 WHIP. In 10 starts on the road, his ERA is 4.72, and his WHIP is 1.48. He allowed two earned runs, six hits and five walks to the Guardians.</p><p>That said, Davis has allowed two runs or fewer in all but four of his 17 starts — all four were on the road. And he has had a few gems on the road, such as his previous road start, when he held the Tigers to one run in six innings with only 77 pitches.</p><p>Starts like those have Davis in the conversation for the All-Star Game, which is scheduled for July 14 in Philadelphia. Rosters will be announced at 6:30 p.m. Saturday on Fox 32.</p><p>But starts like the one Thursday put him in limbo.</p><p>“It was infuriating, to be honest,” said Davis, who felt off from the start. “Just out of sync, fighting against myself, trying to make adjustments on the fly; adjustments weren’t working. Just one of those days you chalk it up to trying to limit as much damage as you can, try to go as deep as you can and try to keep your team in the game.”</p><p>The Sox walked nine in all. After throwing 16 pitches in the eighth, Taylor walked Rhys Hoskins on four pitches to start the ninth, then allowed Rocchio’s homer one out later on a first-pitch fastball that traveled 380 feet and clanged off the right-field foul pole.</p><p>“I wasn’t lining the curveball earlier,” Taylor said. “I was going to stick to my strengths. I had a good fastball, especially to lefties. So I threw a pretty good location, but he was looking for it, got a good swing off.”</p><p>“We talked about coming into this series that limiting the free passes is really No. 1 on the pitching side to beat these guys,” Venable said. “And obviously tonight with the nine walks, you’re just not going to overcome that.”</p><p>Davis entered the game ranked eighth among major-league pitchers with a 3.2 WAR, and he generally has been able to go deep into games — at least as defined by today’s standards. He has thrown at least five innings in 14 starts and at least six innings in 10 starts. But he couldn’t get past the fourth Thursday, exposing a vulnerable bullpen.</p><p>Davis would be the Sox’ first homegrown right-hander to make the All-Star Game since James Baldwin in 2000. The Sox selected Davis, a Texas Tech product, in the 14th round of the 2018 MLB Draft, making him quite a find.</p><p>But if he doesn’t get chosen for the Midsummer Classic, he can look back at his first-half road woes, which cropped up again at an inopportune time — in the opener of a four-game series against the Sox’ first-place competitors in the American League Central. With the loss, the Sox (45-41) fell back into a tie with the Guardians (46-42).</p><p>Davis didn’t face the Guardians last week at Rate Field. With two more series against them — one in August and the other in September — he figures to see them again. By then, perhaps Venable will want to adjust his rotation to ensure that Davis gets a start.</p><div class="PageListL" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" entries.title: Confessions of a WNBA All-Star voter
entries.summary: <p>You know what time it is, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/wnba" target="_blank" >WNBA</a> fans.</p><p>The starters for the All-Star Game were announced Thursday, revealing where fans, players and media ranked the top stars at the midpoint of the season.</p><p>That means everyone gets to indulge their favorite All-Star reactions.</p><p>Pointing out snubs. Stirring the pot on evolving beefs. Exposing fools. Decrying injustice.</p><p>Or maybe, instead of signing up for another round of social-media jousting, you rather would stretch your introspective muscles.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">2026 WNBA All-Star starters are SET 🤩<br><br>See you in the Windy City 🏀🌟 <a href="https://t.co/Zz8waLbfUQ">pic.twitter.com/Zz8waLbfUQ</a></p>— ESPN (@espn) <a href="https://x.com/espn/status/2072730537345614012?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">July 2, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>All-Star debates can be a great opportunity to reflect on ourselves.</p><p>This was my second year as an All-Star voter. I’m still new enough to the process that it can feel imposing, but I’m far enough in to want the ballot to feel authentic. Like a true Alissa Hirsh of the Sun-Times ballot, not just a random media member trying to sound smart.</p><p></p><p>So I decided to lean into my biases.</p><p></p><p>These were the ones I used:</p><p></p><p><b>Hirsh Bias No. 1:</b> The best players from the top six teams were favored. Players from the bottom nine had to clear an extremely high bar. Basketball is a team sport, so team success should matter.</p><p></p><p><b>Hirsh Bias No. 2:</b> Efficient scorers were favored. High-volume scorers with low or mediocre shooting percentages were treated with more suspicion. All the best scorers in the ‘‘W’’ can put points on the board. I wanted to reward the elite group that does it efficiently.</p><p></p><p><b>Hirsh Bias No. 3:</b> Try to represent as many teams as possible. The top teams are really good this year, so I wanted my ballot to reflect that.</p><p></p><p>Now, for the reveal of where my ballot differed from the actual starters.</p><p></p><p>The All-Star guards are Paige Bueckers, Olivia Miles, Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell.</p><p></p><p>I had Bueckers, Miles, Kelsey Plum and Rhyne Howard.</p><p></p><p>The All-Star frontcourt starters are A’ja Wilson, Breanna Stewart, Jessica Shepard, Gabby Williams, Natasha Howard and Aliyah Boston.</p><p></p><p>I had Angel Reese instead of Boston. The rest were the same.</p><p></p><p>Overall, I think my biases served me well. They kept the process simple and fun. And I didn’t stray too far from how the media, fans and players saw things.</p><p></p><p>But they weren’t perfect. Like all biases, I think they narrowed my focus at the expense of larger truths.</p><p></p><p>Leaving off Clark and Boston, in particular, showed my bias toward winning teams was too strong. Despite the Fever’s mediocre record, I should have found space for at least one of them — Clark for her court vision, Boston for her all-around impact — though I’m still not completely sure where.</p><p></p><p>I also realized later that I had been using another bias without fully recognizing it: I was judging players against their own potential, not just against their peers.</p><p></p><p>Plum stuck out to me in part because she is putting together layers of her game that have developed over years. She looks like a player at or near the peak of her powers.</p><p></p><p>That is worth celebrating. I don’t regret the pick.</p><p></p><p>But I also don’t want to leave off deserving players who are having great seasons simply because they are not playing the best basketball of their careers.</p><p></p><p>So what did I learn from all of this?</p><p></p><p>On the surface, being more aware of my biases should make me a better voter next year. On a deeper level, the process also helped me see different parts of myself more clearly.</p><p></p><p>I can see myself wanting to trust my intuition more but still building analytical structures to fall back on.</p><p></p><p>I also can see that, in holding great players to the standard of not just playing well but playing up to their fullest potential, I was doing something I wrote about recently: applying pressure.</p><p></p><p>There it was again, the tendency to bring pressure in place of sentiments that don’t come as naturally but are actually what I’m looking for:</p><p></p><p>Recognition. Appreciation. Even love.</p><p></p><p>At its best, those are the things sports give us the opportunity to practice.</p><p></p><p>We should take that opportunity more often.</p><bsp-list-loadmore class="PageListH" entries.title: Outgoing Chicago FBI chief tells team to 'keep the FBI mission alive' as speculation swirls about his exit
entries.summary: <p>On his way out the door, the<b> </b>man<b> </b>who<b> </b>led<b> </b>the<b> </b>FBI<b> </b>in Chicago<b> </b>for the last two years reminded his team that “being a leader means stepping up when things are hard.”</p><p>In a message addressed to “FBI Chicago,”<b> </b>Douglas<b> </b>DePodesta<b> </b>wrote that “our recent past has challenged us in more ways than most of us could have ever imagined. I’ve never backed down from a fight, as long as it meant our personnel could continue serving the FBI’s mission.</p><p>“Unfortunately,” DePodesta added, “that has proven unpopular over time and my departure is a consequence of that.”</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/politics/2026/07/01/chicago-fbi-chief-depodesta-leaving-unexpectedly-ongoing-credibility-crisis-federal-prosecutors-us-attorney" >Chicago FBI chief leaving unexpectedly, raising eyebrows amid feds’ ongoing credibility crisis</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>The Chicago Sun-Times obtained a copy of DePodesta’s message <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/politics/2026/07/01/chicago-fbi-chief-depodesta-leaving-unexpectedly-ongoing-credibility-crisis-federal-prosecutors-us-attorney" target="_blank" >after news broke</a> that he’d be leaving his job as special agent in charge of the Chicago FBI Field Office. His last day<b> </b>with the FBI<b> </b>will<b> </b>be<b> </b>Monday, the message said.</p><p>DePodesta thanked his team “for the tireless sacrifices you and your families make.</p><p>“No one outside of these walls will ever understand how brave and honorable you each are,” he wrote in closing. “Trust your instincts, be good to one another, and keep the FBI mission alive.”</p><p>In response to reporting about DePodesta’s departure, the<b> </b>FBI<b> </b>Rapid<b> </b>Response<b> </b>social media account on<b> </b>Wednesday<b> </b>said, “It’s simple: Anyone who is not on board with THIS FBI under the leadership of President Trump — which has achieved the lowest murder rate ever — is free to leave.”</p><p>The unexpected departure of DePodesta, a well-respected senior leader, has caused further tumult in Chicago's federal law enforcement community, as well as a flurry of speculation about what prompted it. It comes six weeks after the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/06/27/broadview-six-boutros-chicago" target="_blank" >collapse of the “Broadview Six” case</a> against a Sullivan</a><b> </b>is<b> </b>a<b> </b>1964<b> </b>decision<b> </b>by the U.S. Supreme Court<b> </b>that found damages<b> </b>cannot<b> </b>be awarded<b> </b>to<b> </b>a<b> </b>public<b> </b>official<b> </b>for<b> </b>defamation<b> </b>relating<b> </b>to<b> </b>his<b> </b>official<b> </b>conduct<b> </b>unless<b> </b>he<b> </b>proves<b> </b>that<b> </b>the<b> </b>statement<b> </b>was<b> </b>made<b> </b>with<b> </b>knowledge<b> </b>of<b> </b>its<b> </b>falsehood<b> </b>or<b> </b>with<b> </b>reckless<b> </b>disregard<b> </b>for<b> </b>whether<b> </b>it<b> </b>was<b> </b>true.</p><p>DePodesta took the helm of the FBI’s Chicago Field Office<b> </b>in<b> </b>August<b> </b>2024. He’s been with the FBI since 2002, and over the course of his career he’s worked investigations<b> </b>involving<b> </b>drugs, corruption, terrorism and foreign counterintelligence.</p><p>Before joining the FBI he worked as a police officer in Cincinnati.</p><p>Asked about DePodesta’s departure on Thursday, Boutros told reporters it “was news to me.” He said he had lunch<b> </b>plans<b> </b>with DePodesta<b> </b>on<b> </b>Tuesday, and he said he hopes DePodesta doesn’t cancel “so we can do lunch together.”</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/06/30/trump-ufc-attack-iniguez-mercado" >Chicago man linked to alleged plot to attack White House UFC event ordered held in jail</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>Boutros also praised<b> </b>DePodesta<b> </b>for helping bring <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/06/26/trump-white-house-ufc-attack-chicago" target="_blank" >obstruction of justice charges</a> against<b> </b>a Chicago man<b> </b>accused of playing a role<b> </b>in an alleged plan<b> </b>to attack the<b> </b>June 14<b> </b>Ultimate Fighting Championship event<b> </b>held at the White House on President Donald Trump’s birthday.</p><p>“That case would not have been brought here in Chicago without the work and the dedication of Doug DePodesta and his team,” Boutros said.</p><p>Robert<b> </b>Cekada, director<b> </b>of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, also appeared at the press conference. He told reporters he’d had an opportunity to see DePodesta on Thursday and<b> </b>“thank him for his service and his contribution to our success over the years.”</p><p>Cekada<b> </b>called DePodesta “a great man, honorable man, leaving the Department of Justice and moving on to the next chapter in his life.”<b> </b>And, he said, “that will come for me too.”</p>
